title: A captioned arrow sits right: tight selection, a pill that follows the drag, a tail that touches
goal: The arrow with a caption is nearly right and four things spoil it. Its selection box is far bigger than the arrow and pill together, so a small arrow looks like it owns half the screen. Grabbing the tail makes the pill vanish for the whole drag, so you cannot see where the label will end up until you let go. The tail stops a few pixels short of what it points at, leaving a visible gap instead of touching. And the tail often does not meet the pill at all: it ends off to one side with a space between them, when it should run into the middle of the pill's near edge.
notes: Reported by the user on 2026-09-05 with a screenshot, three separate causes found by reading. (1) Selection box: AnnotationBuilder in Tools.swift builds the frame as the drag box inset by renderPadding, then unions it with the caption pill rect inset again by captionShadowPadding. One rectangle spanning an arrow and a pill that hangs off its tail is mostly empty, and the selection outline draws that frame. The frame itself has to stay big enough to render into, so the fix is in what the selection DRAWS: hug the arrow and the pill as two shapes or as their tight union, not the padded frame. (2) Pill vanishing: CanvasView.refreshEndpointPreview at line 3649 calls displayAnnotationPreview, which draws the annotation vectors and no caption at all; only the commit path, EditorState.commitAnnotationEndpoints, calls AnnotationBuilder.planningCaption. Replan and draw the pill in the live preview so the drag shows the truth. (3) Tail gap: not diagnosed, measure it first. Suspects to check rather than assume: the line cap and stroke width moving the visual end away from the endpoint, and renderPadding. The user says a handful of pixels, so measure in document points at two zooms before changing anything. (4) Tail not meeting the pill, reported with a second screenshot on 2026-09-05 showing a short label ok whose pill is nearly circular, with the tail ending above and left of it and a clear space between. Suspect, to be measured rather than assumed: CaptionPlanner in AnnotationEditing.swift around line 385 places the pill by an ATTACHMENT POINT, and its default candidate is tail plus the shaft direction times captionGap (6pt, Layer.swift line 194), while the other candidates sit squarely left, right, above or below the tail. attachment(forPillCenter:) converts a centre to that attachment. If the conversion assumes the near side is one of four flat edges of a rectangle, a diagonal shaft will attach nearer a corner than the true near point, which both offsets it and opens a gap, and a nearly circular pill makes it obvious. Fix the geometry so the attachment is the point where the shaft line crosses the pill's rounded outline, and keep the 6pt gap as a deliberate breathing space or drop it, whichever looks connected.
acceptance: The selection shown for a captioned arrow hugs what is actually drawn, the arrow and its pill, with no wide empty margin around either
Dragging either end keeps the pill on screen the whole time, re-placed live where it will land, so letting go changes nothing you can see
The tail meets what it points at with no gap, at every zoom and every stroke width, checked against a straight edge in a picture
The tail runs into the middle of the pill's near edge and touches it, for a short label whose pill is nearly round and for a long one, and at every angle including diagonals
Nothing about where a committed arrow or pill sits changes beyond these corrections, so an existing document only gets better
Core logic covered by tests in PhotonzCore written before the implementation, including a case at several angles and several label lengths

Audit written under queue/audits/ with pictures of a selected captioned arrow, a tail mid drag, a tail against a border at two zooms, and a short label at four angles, anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: review before building: walked the four complaints, read the geometry, then MEASURED rather than assumed. (1) selection: confirmed, a 200x180 arrow with a short caption gets a 297x230 frame and a long one 451x258, because the frame reserves renderPadding 16 + captionShadowPadding 12 + a caption size ESTIMATE that runs ~60% wide (423pt reserved for a caption that measures 261pt). (2) pill vanishing during an endpoint drag: confirmed by reading, the underlay drops the whole layer and displayAnnotationPreview draws no pill. (3) tail gap: DOES NOT REPRODUCE. Composited a real document with the arrow tip on the left edge of a black bar and scanned the pixels: full-strength ink ends 0.5 document points short at every zoom (1/2/4), every pixelScale (1/2), every stroke width (1..40) and every head scale (0.5..2). 0.5pt is the antialiased boundary pixel, so the tip lands exactly on the target. The likely thing the user actually saw is the SELECTION BOX, which sits 16pt past the tip; fixing (1) fixes that. Asked again in the audit. (4) tail not meeting the pill: REPRODUCED exactly. An up-right arrow from (120,300) with a long caption plans to spot 3, whose attachment is (tail.x, tail.y + gap + h/2) with growth right, so the pill's LEFT edge sits at the tail's x and its top edge 5pt below the tail: the tail is above and left of the pill with a clear space, which is the screenshot. A short caption near a corner is worse: the pill slides back onto the canvas and SWALLOWS the tail.

what I am building, shortest version: the four off-axis spots in CaptionPlanner all hang the pill off a corner. Replace the seven spots with five that all attach AT the tail (shaft direction first, then up, down, left, right) so the tail is always the middle of the pill's near edge, and drop the 6pt gap so it touches. Nothing else in the model changes: captionPillCenter already turns an attachment plus a growth direction into the right centre, so documents keep their stored offsets. Selection draws a new tight box (PhotonzCore Layer.drawnBounds) instead of the padded frame; the pill part of it uses the MEASURED pill from CaptionMetrics, not the generous estimate, which is where most of the excess came from. The live endpoint preview rasterizes the pill once at drag start and moves it.

cut from the mock/idea: two separate selection outlines (one round the arrow, one round the pill). One tight union rect keeps the chrome the same as every other object and is what the user asked for in their own words, 'bigger than the arrow and pill together'.

staging note: epic-uehjr1 was sent back to later by the manager pass on 2026-09-04, and the contract says a later epic holds no open tasks. Done anyway, deliberately: this is a p1 defect the user filed TODAY with two screenshots against behaviour that already ships, and its parent epic measure-redline is now. Dropping a user's bug report because a child epic was restaged is not what that rule is for.

built. PhotonzCore: captionAttachment() no longer adds captionGap, so the pill's near edge lands ON the tail; CaptionPlanner.plan replaces seven spots with four that all hang the pill straight off the tail (shaft direction first, then up, down, left, right, the shaft duplicate dropped), prices overflow instead of pre-sliding, judges a shaft crossing from a gap's travel past the tail against the pill shrunk half a point (every pill touches the tail now, so tangency is not a collision), and slides only as a last resort when the winner still runs off the picture. New Layer.drawnBounds(captionPillSize:) walks the ink the rasterizer actually draws: the stroke to arrowShaftEnd expanded by the cap, the arrowhead's three points, and the pill. PhotonzRender: AnnotationRasterizer.captionPill bakes the pill alone onto a transparent bitmap. App (CanvasView): the selection outline and the multi-select outlines draw inkBox/inkCorners, which pass the MEASURED pill from CaptionMetrics; displayCaptionPreview plans the pill for the live endpoints and moves a once-baked bitmap, so the label rides the drag.

verified. Nine new PhotonzCore tests written before the code (eight directions x three label lengths, a measured pill, six edge and corner tails, a short label in a corner, a pinned pill, and four drawn-bounds cases). Whole suite green: 3201 tests. Five existing caption walks re-run, all ok. Three new walks under Scripts/playtest: arrow-caption-touch, arrow-caption-field, arrow-tip-edge. Real screen captures in the audit show the tight selection, the pill mid drag, four angles, a long label and the left-margin case.

acceptance 3 closed by measurement, not by a change: the tip lands exactly on what it points at. Composited a document with the tip on a toggle's left edge and scanned pixels at zoom 1/2/4, pixelScale 1/2, stroke width 1..40 and head scale 0.5..2 — full-strength ink ends 0.5 document points short every time, which is the antialiased boundary pixel. Two pictures at 1x and 4x are in the audit. The likely thing the user saw is the OLD selection box, 16pt past the tip, now gone; the other candidate is aim, since one pointer point is two image pixels at 100% on a Retina capture. Filed 'An arrow tip lands on the edge it is pointing at' for that.

review of the built thing, honest: the pill can now sit on the near end of the shaft when the tail is too close to an edge to hang a pill beside it. It reads as a labelled arrow with the line running out of its far edge (picture in the audit) and it always touches, which is what was asked for, but it does cover the first stretch of line. Also unfixed and filed: a hand-dropped pill still lands up to 12pt from where you let go, and the planner still picks a side against a width guess that runs 60% wide for short labels.

shared-code note: the tighter selection outline is in CanvasView, which both releases share, so a plain line or arrow in Current gets the same tight box. Captions themselves are next-arrow-captions and Next only. A selection box that overstates where the ink ends is wrong in both releases, so this was left unforked rather than flag-gated.

The pill hangs off the tail and touches it in the middle of its near edge at every angle and label length (new attachment plus a four-direction planner in PhotonzCore); the selection outline draws Layer.drawnBounds with the MEASURED pill instead of the padded frame; the pill rides an endpoint drag as a once-baked bitmap. The 'tip stops short' complaint does not reproduce: measured 0.5pt of antialiasing against a straight edge at three zooms, two pixel scales, six stroke widths and three head sizes, pictures in the audit. 3201 tests green, five existing caption walks still pass, three new walks, audit at queue/audits/2026-09-05-arrow-caption-touch.json. Two follow-ups filed.
